R056-01.notes: B covers both halves: courtship code (P1-2) and Photuris exploitation plus male response (P3-5). A: light chemistry never discussed; the only chemicals are defensive ones. C: P4 presents deliberate choice as disputed, so the passage does not argue for it. D: birds and spiders are mentioned only once, as fireflies' predators.

flags.note: D ('repeats his own flash pattern exactly and immediately') is meant to be ruled out by 'immediately', but an immediate reply is also a reply at the wrong interval, since females answer 'after a precise delay'. A careful student could argue D also describes a reply that makes a male keep flying. A is the direct paraphrase and clearly best. Consider changing D to something that cannot be read as a timing mismatch.

R056-02.notes: P2: 'A male who sees a flash at the wrong interval is likely to keep flying.' B: brightness is never mentioned. C: perching on a leaf below is the normal position of a correct female, so it is not a reason to keep flying. D: pattern repetition is not discussed; see flag.

R056-03.notes: P3: 'Because the code is so specific, it can be exploited'; males respond to 'the right response at the right delay.' A: males do see females below (P2). B: contradicted, because males ignore wrong-interval replies. D: males are deceived; they do not prefer Photuris females.

R056-04.notes: P3: the prey carry defensive chemicals that make fireflies distasteful to spiders and birds, and Photuris females take them in. A: the mimicry is not acquired by eating. B: pigments are not mentioned. C: eggs are not mentioned.

R056-05.notes: The detail explains why the prey is their source of chemical defense. B: nothing says they are easier to catch, and the point is that they gain protection. C: relatedness is not discussed. D: misapplies 'these chemicals' to light production; the females clearly do flash.

R056-06.notes: P4: the cautious biologists say switching may be 'less a matter of deliberate choice than of a simple rule.' A: both groups accept that the switching happens. C: the eating is not disputed. D: male discrimination is not part of this disagreement.

R056-07.notes: 'Exploited' means taken advantage of or used for one's own ends; 'manipulated' is the closest choice, since Photuris uses the code to deceive. A (explored) and D (explained) are neutral senses that do not fit. B (destroyed): the code continues to function. 'Manipulated' is a slightly loose synonym, but it is clearly the best of the four.

R056-08.notes: P5 sets up a tradeoff: fast approach means finding mates sooner but a higher risk of being eaten, so slow testing trades mating speed for safety. A: they are testing replies, which is the opposite of being unable to recognize them. B: there is no imitation by males. C: interest in mating is not the explanation; caution is.

R056-09.notes: 'As if' signals an interpretation, not an established fact. B: 'prove' overstates. C: no laboratory experiment is described ('in some populations'). D: confusing the females is not suggested; the males are checking the reply.

R056-10.notes: The final sentence echoes the opening 'apparent randomness' and sums up courtship, deception, appetite, and caution. A: the items listed were all discussed earlier. B: intelligence is not compared. D: it says the randomness only seems to be there, which is the opposite of admitting the flashes are random.
